**A10 fix-direction FORK posted (#297) — Option A measured green but emits [FAIL-SHA] on the good citizen; recommended C**

**What**: Ruling rev 8 made A10 a **blocker on the STACK'S MERGE** (not its review, not a separate issue) via finding `I297-A10-STACK-REGRESSION`, and required the PATCHER to write a `## FORK` for the fix direction. Fork posted (#297 comment 5039868713). No fix committed; `fa3a922` unchanged.

**Reviewer's blocker framing, premise VERIFIED by me before accepting**: A10 is a fail-open the stack INTRODUCES, not one it inherits. Checked `git show origin/feature/v2.0.0:brain/scripts/brain-audit.mjs` → `[SKIP]` appears only for "before audit baseline" and "no parent" — **zero exemption machinery on the base**, so the A10 chain FAILS there (safe). (`resolution.mjs` DOES exist on base with 6 exports — that's PR2b/#294 — but brain-audit doesn't consume it for skips.)

**MEASURED, all three implemented + run + reverted:**

- **Option A** — `--diff-filter=A` → `--diff-filter=AM` (touched = added ∪ modified must be absent at tip). Closes A10, full suite **1822/1822**. **BUT the measured cost is worse than estimated**: a legitimate modify-shaped tip-most cleanup reverter loses its exemption and emits `[FAIL-SHA]` — the auto-revert signal — **on the good citizen**. PR4 would revert the cleanup and RESURRECT the payload. That is exactly the harm §15.5 names ("never revert the intermediate legit reverter"), reappearing on the emission path after being closed on the skip path.
- **Option B** — pure-deletion-only exemption. Closes A10 but reddens `addedPathsAbsentAt — the audited tip is the anchor` (1822/1821/1): it makes the tip irrelevant, un-converting the §2.2 precondition MINOR 1 just turned into code. **Strictly dominated by A.**
- **Option C (RECOMMENDED)** — Option A + withhold `[FAIL-SHA]` when the failure survives only through the modify-shaped denial. Costs real machinery (thread the denial reason from the exemption site to the emission block) + a new frozen fixture the FINDER must write first.

**KEY TECHNICAL FINDING — one of my own three shapes COLLAPSED under measurement**: "content-level liveness of the candidate's own change" is **degenerate for every tip-most merge** — the tip-most candidate's change is live at the tip BY DEFINITION. It reproduces the exact rev-3 `isResolvedAt` failure that broke A2/A6. `(c′)` only escapes this because a pure delete has no added paths and passes **VACUOUSLY**, not because it measures liveness successfully. Recorded as an elimination on the thread rather than quietly dropped. **Generalizes: any "did my change survive to the tip" test denies every tip-most reverter.**

**Where the fix lands follows the ruling**: Option A is one line → PR3b absorbs it; Option C is its own reviewable unit → wants PR3c.

**Standing**: #298/#299 reviewable now, mergeable only with A10 closed on the stack. A10 fixture joins the stack (cherry-picked/rebased onto the fix commit) once the direction is ruled, frozen and untouched.</content>
